title: The Last Aeronaut
author: Marina Blackwood
description: A scrappy airship mechanic must keep a failing dirigible aloft long enough to reach safety.

sections.text: The airship Meridian groans as a boiler valve blows, venting steam across the deck. Land is still hours away.

options.description: Rush to patch the boiler yourself

sections.text: You climb into the engine room, wrench in hand, steam scalding the air around you.

consequence.text: The hot metal burns your palms before you get a grip.

options.description: Use the wrench instead of your bare hands

consequence.text: The wrench keeps your hands clear of the worst of the heat.

sections.text: The captain wakes instantly, tossing you a pair of thick gloves before you head below deck together.

options.description: Patch the valve with the captain's help

consequence.text: With the gloves and an extra pair of hands, the work goes smoothly.

options.description: Send the captain to steady the helm and handle it alone

consequence.text: Working alone, the steam catches you off guard more than once.

sections.text: The valve holds, but the boiler pressure is still climbing. A safety release lever sits just out of easy reach.

consequence.text: You strain hard to reach it, and something in your shoulder protests.

options.description: Vent pressure through the emergency stack instead

consequence.text: The safer option costs you nothing but a little time.

sections.text: You reach the lever just in time. The pressure drops, and the Meridian limps safely into port.
Steam roars through the emergency stack, and the ship steadies. Cheers erupt on deck as land comes into view.
